Yet per reference memory, baseline shifts monotonically due to global trend: from ref 0 (median −1.30 at index ~0) to ref 3 (median +1.12 at index ~2390–2879), slope ≈0.000936 implies expected median at index 1702 ≈ −1.30 + 1702×0.000936 ≈ −1.30 + 1.593 ≈ +0.293; at 1995: −1.30 + 1995×0.000936 ≈ −1.30 + 1.867 ≈ +0.567. Observed values (~−0.6) are ~1.2 units below expectation—far exceeding local slope-induced variation (≤0.275 over 3P). This confirms a true level shift inconsistent with global trend extrapolation. Morphology, period, amplitude scaling, and smoothness match normal pattern, so anomaly type is trend (regime-level offset), not shapelet or frequency. Confidence remains high (0.92 → 0.90) as contrast is decisive and no benign explanation (phase, truncation, noise) fits. Zoomed plot shows continuous linear ramp across full [2402,2996]; slope appears uniform (~0.000936), not steeper. Correct slope matches canonical 0.000936 when aligned to global trend. Thus candidate 1 is a false positive: the segment is part of the same depressed regime as candidate 0, but the proposed ‘steeper slope’ is an artifact of using wrong reference baseline. Since candidate 0 already covers the core anomalous depression, and candidate 1’s boundaries extend beyond the visually coherent event (the red band ends near 2000 in first plot, and second plot shows no distinct break at 2402), candidate 1 is removed.
